title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a formal scheme, smooth over W, with a Frobenius lift σ. A Dieudonné-type F-crystal on S_0 = S mod p is represented on a trivial module E_S by two pieces of data. A is the connection matrix, ∇ = d + A. F_M is the Frobenius, given by a matrix Φ, mapping σ*M to M. There is also an 'inverse' Ψ with ΦΨ = p^r, i.e. a Verschiebung or isogeny condition.

1) Morphisms. A morphism u: M → M' is horizontal iff u∘A = du + A'∘u, i.e. du = u∘A − A'∘u. It commutes with Frobenius iff F_{M'}·u^σ = u·F_M, where u^σ = F_S^*(u).

2) Example, invertible modules (rank one). The data are φ ∈ Γ(O_S) and ω ∈ Γ(Ω̂^1_{S/W}), subject to:
- dω = 0 (integrability);
- dφ = φ(ω^σ − ω), where ω^σ = σ*ω (horizontality of Frobenius);
- φψ = p^r (φ is invertible in A[1/p]).
Two such objects (φ,ω) and (φ',ω') are isomorphic iff there is a unit u ∈ Γ(O_S^*) with ω' − ω = −du/u and φ'/φ = u/u^σ.

3) Classification. Isomorphism classes are therefore the H^1 of a three-term complex of multiplicative groups (or monoids):
Γ(O_S^*) → Γ(Ω̂^1) × Γ(O_S ∩ A[1/p]^*) → Γ(Ω^2) × Γ(Ω^1)[1/p]
The first map is u ↦ (∓dlog u, u/u^σ); the second is (φ,ω) ↦ (dω, dlog φ − (ω^σ − ω)).
In modern terms this is a multiplicative 'syntomic/Deligne-type' cone: the cone of (dlog, 1 − σ) on the multiplicative de Rham complex. It computes rank-one F-crystals on an affine S with a Frobenius lift.

The page belongs to Grothendieck's 1970 working notes on Dieudonné crystals and Barsotti–Tate groups. The neighbouring page is a draft on semistable reduction and Barsotti–Tate groups.
errors: Sign inconsistency: with the derived rule ω' − ω = −du/u, the first differential should be u ↦ (−du/u, u/u^σ). As written, (du/u, u/u^σ) does not compose to zero with the second map; with the minus sign it does.

The middle term Γ(O_S)^! (elements invertible in A[1/p]) is only a monoid, not a group, so 'classes de cohomologie' must be read as orbits of a monoid action. Taking global sections presupposes S affine (or that the crystal is trivialised).
The exponent r in φψ = p^r is implicitly a fixed integer, i.e. constant slope on connected S.

ideas.what: Description of F-crystals on a formal lift with Frobenius lift as (module, integrable connection, horizontal Frobenius), and morphisms as horizontal Frobenius-compatible maps
ideas.modern_name: F-crystals / Dieudonné crystals via connections and Frobenius lifts
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (ICM Nice 1970); Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1970, publ. 1974)

ideas.what: Classification of rank-one F-crystals by H^1 of the complex O^* → Ω^1 × O[1/p]^* → Ω^2 × Ω^1[1/p]
ideas.modern_name: multiplicative syntomic / Deligne–Beilinson-type cone; rank-one F-(iso)crystals
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Katz (unit-root F-crystals, 1973), Fontaine–Messing (syntomic, 1987) for related cones

deep.surprise_reason: Routine working computation of rank-one F-crystals in coordinates. The cone formulation anticipates syntomic-type complexes in spirit, but it is standard and elementary.
